correctness.rationale: Affinely distinct line directions form q+1 parallel classes of q lines. Two lines meet iff directions differ; the line flagification is the join of their q-point discrete complexes. Reduced homology of each factor is integral augmentation lattice of rank q−1. Integral join Künneth yields only H_q as their tensor; exchanging odd suspended factors contributes a sign, giving the canonical signed affine-group action. Trace of tensor factor cycles equals composite fixed-line trace f_C−1, proving the full character. A nonzero translation fixes exactly the q lines parallel to its own direction and none in the other q directions, giving (q−1)(−1)^q. On the unflagified point side, line-simplex intersections are at most vertices, so each line simplex may be contracted to the incidence graph; explicitly H1 is the kernel of the direct sum line augmentations mapping to the point lattice. Connected incidence graph has q²(q+1) edges and 2q²+q vertices, cycle rank μ=(q−1)²(q+1); its translation Lefschetz character is 1−q off identity. When q odd, nonidentity traces agree, so character difference is r times regular representation; Fourier inversion yields the supplied multiplicities. Reconstructed finite affine planes q=2,3,5, line orientations and all translation character checks directly; q=4 source checked via published checker text, not independently enumerated in this run. Universal claims are proven by the exact join and graph-cycle logic, not q<=5 data.
